local_review.finding_body: The added tests/src/com.squareup.okhttp3/okhttp/3.9.0/src/test/java/android/security/NetworkSecurityPolicy.java shadowed a real Android framework type, and AndroidPlatformTest depended on that fake type to activate an Android-only library path on the desktop test runtime. The contribution also changed the inherited X509TrustManagerExtensions stub to force the desired fallback. This violates FS-test-contract.2.3 and adds unrelated synthetic coverage to a javac repair rather than narrowly adapting the failing TrustRootIndex call.
local_review.finding_title: Generated repair uses a shadow Android API to manufacture coverage
local_review.fix_note: Removed the newly added fake-dependent Android scenario and its filter entry, restored the inherited X509TrustManagerExtensions behavior, and reduced TrustRootIndexTest to the minimal 3.9.0 API adaptation through Platform.buildTrustRootIndex while preserving the original reflective trust-manager behavior and assertions. Forge finalization regenerated the resulting statistics.
local_review.review_comment: Reviewed the target-coordinate-only diff, local gate evidence, test-contract musts, cheating patterns, and repair coverage. After repair, overall dynamic access is 24/28 versus 25/25 (a 14.29 percentage-point drop, within the 20-point large-report limit); reflection passes because covered calls remain 24, and the removed resources scope passes as 0/0. The exact Forge finalization command then passed current-defaults, future-defaults-all, and GraalVM 25 test lanes plus metadata, formatting, Checkstyle, generated-test, and statistics checks, and a second complete run made no publishable change.
